subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — AtlasHealth initial recap and asks
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Moreno <jessica.moreno@atlashealth.com>, AtlasHealth CloudOps <cloudops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — AtlasHealth initial recap and asks

Hi Jessica / CloudOps team,

Thanks for the time today — this note pulls together what we heard on the call and the concrete asks to evaluate dedicated/reserved GPU pools for AtlasHealth. I wrote this so we have a single place to align on scope and next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- Variable inference spikes during business hours (esp. 11:00–14:00 PT) causing queued requests and >1s p95 for realtime scoring.
- Cost unpredictability on current cloud endpoints; finance needs a committed predictable spend for next FY.
- Data isolation requirement for certain PHI workloads (must run in a dedicated pool, VPC-isolated).

Current stack (what you told us)
- Models: two transformer encoders used for document classification (1.2B and 7B quantized variants).
- Hosting: GCP (private project, VPC-native), Kubernetes-based serving today with custom autoscaler for CPU-backed tasks.
- Traffic shape: bursty, with 200–600 TPS at minute granularity during peaks; baseline ~40 TPS off-peak.

Success criteria for a Dedicated pilot
- Stable p95 latency <= 300ms for the 1.2B model at 200 TPS sustained.
- Predictable monthly committed spend for reserved GPU pools + transparent burst usage accounting.
- VPC isolation + customer-managed KMS for keys; SOC2-compliant audit logs.

Initial assessment / our recommendations
- Reserved GPU pool sized for steady-state + a controlled burst window (we recommend reserving capacity for ~250 sustained TPS and enabling burst policy to cover up to 600 TPS for short windows).
- Autoscale policy: scale by active inference slots with a fast up-scaler (30s) and slower downscale window (5m) to avoid thrash.
- Quantization: run 7B as an int8 variant in the dedicated pool to reduce footprint; keep 1.2B with optimized kernels for latency.

Concrete asks from AtlasHealth (what we need to size pilot)
1) Sample traffic (CSV): per-minute request counts for last 14 days, annotated by model type if possible. See attached template: traffic_sample_template.csv
2) Representative payload sizes and typical input lengths (tokens) for both models.
3) Any regulatory constraints for the pilot (e.g., must be in specific GCP region, additional encryption controls).
4) A technical POC contact (SRE level) and availability for a 60–90min deep-dive this week.

Planned next steps
- You: share sample traffic and token length examples (ideally by Tue, Mar 2).
- Us: produce a short sizing sketch (GPU types, pool size, cost estimates) and a pilot timeline once we have traffic.
- Book a technical workshop to validate KV/cache sizing and autoscale thresholds.

Attachments: traffic_sample_template.csv (CSV), redwood_security_checklist_v1.pdf (PDF)

If anything above is off, please flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll plan to put the sizing note together as soon as we get the traffic sample.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference for production

Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — AtlasHealth initial recap and asks

Thanks Grace — this is great and matches what we discussed. Quick clarifications and I've attached our traffic export.

- The 200–600 TPS window is correct; the peak spikes are usually short (1–10 minutes) but happen multiple times per day.
- Payloads: doc OCR outputs average ~420 tokens; some longer reports hit ~1,200 tokens but that's <1% of traffic.
- Models: the 7B is currently pruned/quantized for inference; we included the binary size in the traffic file.

Attachment: atlas_traffic_14d.csv (contains per-minute counts and model mapping)

We also have a preliminary security note: pilot must run in our eu-central1 project for regulated datasets (we can whitelist a single region). Can the dedicated pool be region-locked?

Jessica

Director, ML Platform | AtlasHealth
jessica.moreno@atlashealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity discovery — AtlasHealth initial recap and asks

Fwding Jessica's traffic export. Quick tech notes for Rishi / infra folks:

- Traffic shape: per-minute spikes up to ~600 TPS, but 99th percentile spike duration ~7 minutes. That argues for modest reserved footprint + burst buckets rather than fully provisioned N GPUs.
- Region constraint: eu-central1 for regulated datasets — we'll need a dedicated pool in that region (private control plane ok, but control plane connectivity must be from our management plane).
- Models: 1.2B and 7B (quantized) — estimate ~12–16 inferences/sec per A100-40 for the 1.2B depending on batching; 7B int8 likely ~3–5 inf/sec per GPU for low-latency path. Need to validate with our kernel set.

Immediate asks from infra team to size pilot properly:
1) Rishi: can you run a quick back-of-envelope mapping (given the CSV) to GPUs and expected concurrency targets? Aim to produce a first-pass sizing doc by Wed, Mar 3.
2) Grace: set up the technical deep-dive with Atlas SRE and schedule the 90min slot; invite product infra and our quant team.
3) I'll prep cost estimates for reserved vs burst usage and a candidate autoscale policy.

Attachment forwarded: atlas_traffic_14d.csv

--
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — AtlasHealth initial recap and asks

Great — thanks for the traffic file and the region note, Jessica. We can run a region-locked reserved pool in eu-central1 for the regulated datasets.

Next steps / scheduling
- Technical deep-dive: propose Wed, Mar 3 at 10:00 CET / 01:00 PT (90 minutes). Agenda: workload shapes, KV/cache sizing, autoscale thresholds, and network/KMS controls. Please confirm or suggest an alternate time. Link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/7b2c2d-tech-deep-dive
- Deliverables from Redwood after deep-dive (target by Fri, Mar 6): sizing sketch (GPU types & counts), pilot cost estimate, and a short runbook for pilot operations.
- Contracting: we can provisionally hold a small reserved pool while legal/workshop finalize terms. If you have a procurement timeline or PO number, share it and we'll align billing windows.

I'll also attach a short checklist we use for region-locked pilots and send a calendar invite once Jessica confirms.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
